title: Ergonomics
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: Construction has one of the highest rates of back injuries of any industry, often from lifting and carrying heavy materials. Use equipment, plan your lifts, and get help.
talking_points: Back injuries come from lifting and carrying heavy materials, working in awkward positions, and bending often to lift from the ground. Construction has one of the highest rates of back injuries of any industry.
Whenever possible, use mechanical equipment like a dolly to move heavy objects horizontally.
Never try to lift an item weighing over 50 pounds by yourself.
Plan your lifts. Make sure the path is clear and you are facing the direction of travel before you lift.
While lifting, tuck in your chin to keep your neck straight, and keep your back as straight as possible.
Lift with your leg muscles, which helps protect your back.
Ask for help with heavy or awkward objects. Coordinate and practice team lifting before you use it to move objects.
Avoid twisting your body while carrying an object. Do not write off back pain as part of the job.
site_hazards_to_check: Heavy bags, blocks, or materials being moved by hand when a cart, dolly, or forklift could do it
Blocked or uneven paths between the pile and the work area
Materials stored on the ground that force repeated bending
Items over 50 pounds that workers plan to lift alone
Awkward loads that need two or more people
discussion_questions: What is the heaviest item we will move today, and what equipment will move it?
How do you plan a lift before you pick something up?
When do you ask for help or use a team lift?
